title: Curated-catalog ids that release v2.1 names differently
accepted_by: akane321 (owner), 2026-09-24: accepted on the implementation agent's acceptance review (all 15 entries match the investigation that found them); not read entry by entry
notes: canned_tomato: `same` as canned_tomatoes AND a `variety` of tomato. The checker requires the look-alike `tomato` to be decided, and canned_tomatoes belongs to WP3, which may not have merged yet; the direct link keeps 'no tomato' working either way and stays true after WP3 links canned_tomatoes to tomato.

ground_cumin: `same` as cumin. Release recipes write cumin as ground cumin or cumin powder far more often than seeds (see --show cumin), so the two ids are one food in practice. A household that avoids whole cumin seed is not modelled.
cherry_tomato: not the fruit `cherry`. It is a small tomato, so it is a variety of tomato only, and excluding tomato removes it but excluding it leaves ordinary tomatoes.

firm_tofu.reason: Pressed, dense tofu, used at 250-300 g in four curated stir-fry, soba and bowl recipes; release v2.1 writes firm tofu as plain tofu (92 recipes), but firm is one kind of it, so it is a variety and not the same id.

soba_noodle.reason: Buckwheat noodles, 160 g in the curated soba dishes; the singular id and release v2.1's soba_noodles are one food under two names, and release recipes write it exactly as soba noodles.

black_bean.reason: Black beans by weight in three curated bowls and stews; release v2.1's black_beans is the same beans, written as black beans in every recipe there, so the singular curated id is only an alias.

canned_tomato.reason: No-added-salt canned tomatoes, 200-800 g in ten curated stews and pastas; the same food as release v2.1's canned_tomatoes, and canned tomato is still tomato for a household that avoids tomatoes.

vegetable_stock.reason: Low-sodium vegetable stock in three curated soups and oats; release v2.1 has vegetable_broth with recipes writing vegetable stock and vegetable broth interchangeably, so stock and broth are one food here.

ground_cumin.reason: Ground cumin at 2 tsp in six curated curries and stews; release v2.1's cumin is mostly written as ground cumin or cumin powder, so the curated id is the same spice and cumin is the canonical id.

salmon_fillet.reason: A 300 g cut of salmon in three curated bowls and trays; a fillet is a part of the fish, so avoiding salmon avoids it, while excluding only salmon_fillet leaves other salmon cuts alone.

canned_tuna.reason: A 185 g tin of tuna in water, used in three curated pasta and rice dishes; it is tuna in tinned form, so a household avoiding tuna avoids it, and it is one form of tuna and not the whole of it.

cherry_tomato.reason: Small sweet tomatoes at 150-160 g in six curated salads and bowls; a variety of tomato, and not the stone fruit cherry that the name also spells.

baby_spinach.reason: Young spinach leaves, 100-150 g raw in nine curated dishes; the same plant as spinach at an earlier stage, so avoiding spinach avoids it, and avoiding baby spinach alone leaves mature spinach.

yellow_onion.reason: One whole yellow onion in five curated stews and curries; the common cooking onion, a colour variety of onion, so anyone avoiding onion avoids it but excluding it leaves red or white onion.

red_lentil.reason: Split red lentils at 180-240 g in three curated soups and curries; a kind of lentil, so avoiding lentils avoids them, while avoiding red lentils leaves brown and green ones.

rolled_oats.reason: Flattened whole oats, 100-140 g in three curated porridge and egg-cake recipes; a form of oats, and release v2.1 writes rolled oats and oats as one ingredient family, so it sits under oats.

greek_yogurt.reason: Plain strained yogurt, 400 g in the curated yogurt oat bowl; a kind of yogurt, so avoiding yogurt avoids it, while avoiding Greek yogurt alone leaves regular yogurt.

wholewheat_pasta.reason: Dried wholewheat pasta, 180 g in four curated pasta dishes; a wheat-flour form of pasta, so avoiding pasta avoids it. Wheat as an allergen is handled by the allergen table, not here.
